ecosystem_findings.summary: Within this source, the proposed lens receives several distinct mechanisms: algebraic dequantization, passage from functions to balanced loci, auxiliary-coordinate contractions, equivalence of presentations, and enrichment by phases before lifting. This is source-level reinforcement only; comparison with the frozen parent and novelty remain unconfirmed.

units.representation_dependency: The bridge depends on logarithmic amoebas, local pair-of-pants models, and phase data that supplement the underlying tropical curve; the tropical skeleton alone is explicitly insufficient.
units.selection_reason: It exposes a useful bridge-construction principle: enrich a coarse piecewise-linear limit with compatible local phase data, then ask whether the enriched object lifts to a classical family; regularity marks the stated success boundary.
units.title: Phases, amoebas, and realizability of tropical curves

units.context_note: This is an applications section. It states, rather than proves, a correspondence between classical and tropical plane-curve counts and illustrates why local intersection multiplicities are essential when the number of visible tropical curves changes with the configuration.
units.representation_dependency: The account depends on tropical moduli, stable intersection, and a cited correspondence theorem. Its conceptual value is the weighted-count mechanism, not an independent derivation of the enumerative result.
units.selection_reason: It shows how a simpler piecewise-linear problem can stand in for a classical one only after solutions receive intrinsic multiplicities, so invariant totals survive changes that alter the unweighted solution set.
units.title: Weighted tropical counts in complex enumerative geometry

units.context_note: This is also application-level survey material. It defines signed real multiplicities and states a cited equality with Welschinger invariants; it does not supply a self-contained proof or a general-purpose construction beyond the enumerative setting.
units.representation_dependency: The mechanism depends on parity, lattice-triangle data, and a classical-to-tropical correspondence specific to real curve counts; it should not be generalized beyond that setting without further evidence.
units.selection_reason: It gives a second, distinct invariance mechanism: individual real solution counts vary, but local signs and zero contributions compress geometric behavior into a deformation-stable total.
units.title: Signed multiplicities for invariant real curve counts
